title: To what extent is ChatGPT useful for language teacher lesson plan creation?
extended_summary:
This paper examines whether ChatGPT can be used to generate effective foreign-language teacher lesson plans and how prompt specificity affects the quality and consistency of the outputs. The authors frame the problem as a practical and research gap: teachers increasingly need support for lesson planning, but it is unclear how reliable generative AI is when used for this purpose, especially when prompted in simple, zero-shot ways.

The intervention/approach was not a human-subjects intervention but an experimental prompt-evaluation study using ChatGPT 4.0. The authors created five zero-shot prompts that progressively increased in specificity for a 45-minute high school Level I Spanish lesson on a Costa Rican restaurant. Each prompt was run in 10 separate chats, producing 50 lesson plans that were scored against a 25-item rubric based on best practices and edTPA-aligned lesson criteria. The rubric and context were derived from teacher-education expectations at the University of North Carolina at Charlotte.

The study context is K-12 teacher preparation, specifically foreign language teacher education in the United States, with the sample materials centered on a high school Spanish classroom. The paper does not study students directly; instead, it evaluates AI-generated materials intended for preservice and practicing teachers. Findings suggest ChatGPT can produce generally strong lesson plans, but added specificity does not reliably improve quality in a linear way. Including a lesson template sometimes reduced quality, while including explicit scoring criteria improved outputs most. Outputs also showed substantial non-determinism, with the same prompt producing lesson plans that varied widely in quality.

The authors conclude that ChatGPT can be useful for lesson-plan creation, but teachers must critically review and revise generated materials because outputs may include outdated pedagogical practices and inconsistent inclusion of key instructional components such as cultural connections and communicative interaction.

identified_tools.name: ChatGPT
identified_tools.description: OpenAI's generative AI chatbot / large language model system used for conversational text generation and prompting-based assistance.
identified_tools.use_case: Used to generate foreign language teacher lesson plans from five zero-shot prompts of increasing specificity; each prompt was run 10 times to assess prompt specificity, output variability, and alignment with lesson-plan criteria.

findings.finding_summary: Across 50 ChatGPT-generated lesson plans (5 prompts � 10 iterations), increasing prompt specificity had a marginal effect on overall rubric scores (p=0.0442; F=2.668; DF=4), but pairwise tests were not significant after correction. The mean score did not increase linearly: P.2 averaged 21.2/25, P.3 19.8/25, P.4 19.6/25, and P.5 21.6/25.

ChatGPT outputs showed substantial non-determinism within identical prompts. For example, P.1 outputs ranged from 16/25 to 23/25 and P.5 from 20/25 to 25/25, with outputs from the same prompt varying by at least five rubric elements. Distances and clustering showed only partial separation by prompt group, indicating both convergence and divergence across repeated runs.
findings.measure: Within-prompt variability in rubric scores and Jaccard-distance similarity of output components

findings.finding_summary: Several lesson-plan components were consistently present, including meaningful context, teacher input aligned to objectives, and activities appropriate to proficiency level. Other components were inconsistently or weakly represented, including cultural connections and integration of ACTFL standards; some prompt features (especially the checklist in P.5) improved inclusion of required elements, while template-only prompting sometimes reduced quality in specific sections such as the warm-up and teacher input.
findings.measure: Presence/absence of 25 rubric criteria across generated lesson plans

quality_tier_rationale: This is a single-study, mixed-methods/quantitative evaluation of ChatGPT outputs rather than a controlled effectiveness trial. The design is systematic and transparent, but it does not establish causal impacts on teacher or student outcomes.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper reports some meaningful improvements in rubric alignment with stronger prompting, but effects are modest and inconsistent, with substantial variability across repeated outputs. No effect sizes were reported, and the main results are about output quality rather than downstream educational impact.
